original_poem:
ہم دیکھیں گے  
لازم ہے کہ ہم بھی دیکھیں گے  
وہ دن کہ جس کا وعدہ ہے  
جو لوحِ ازل میں لکھا ہے  
جب ظلم و ستم کے کوہ گراں  
روئی کی طرح اڑ جائیں گے  
ہم محکوموں کے پاؤں تلے  
یہ دھرتی دھڑ دھڑ دھڑکے گی  
اور اہلِ حکم کے سر اوپر  
جب بجلی کڑ کڑ کڑکے گی  
ہم دیکھیں گے
translated_poem:
We shall see  
It is certain that we too shall see  
The day that has been promised  
Which is written on the slate of eternity  
When the mountains of tyranny and oppression  
Will float away like cotton  
Beneath our feet—the feet of the oppressed—  
This earth will throb and beat  
And over the heads of the rulers  
Lightning will crack and strike  
We shall see

stanzas.loss_note: لوحِ ازل (lauh-e-azal, the primordial tablet) carries a specific Quranic-Sufi resonance — the divine record inscribed before creation — which 'slate of eternity' approximates but flattens into a generic philosophical image, losing the theological weight of divine promise as cosmic inevitability.

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: the promised day of justice as divinely pre-ordained, inscribed before time itself — making revolution a theological certainty, not merely a political hope

metaphor_spans.abstract_meaning: the sudden, effortless dissolution of seemingly permanent oppressive power
the earth's pulse as the collective heartbeat of the oppressed reclaiming their ground
divine or revolutionary retribution striking down the heads of rulers

cultural_entities.translation_note: Quranic-Sufi concept of the primordial divine tablet — the source of all pre-ordained decree — reduced to 'slate of eternity', losing its theological specificity.
Rendered as 'the oppressed', which captures the political register adequately.
Rendered as 'the rulers'; the Urdu phrase carries a more formal, legalistic weight — those who hold the authority of command.
